note: The starting point every run begins from. The world at this commit, and these briefings. Changing either means a new seed version, because runs from different seeds are not comparable. The world repository is squashed to a single root at each seed, so a run cannot read the history of the run before it.
changedFromV1: the engine claims a command only when something came of it
world data changes are read in without disconnecting anyone
creatures return, and a newly written creature is not wiped
the terminal gives its input back after a reconnect
the living world and the world file named as different things
the briefing no longer says where the edges of its reach are
reach: everything the world is made of
changedFromV2: naming what you are fighting attacks it
half an item's name is enough
an action no handler implements is refused by the validator, by name
an action's scope is visible to anything that reads an interaction
a reset forgets the world's files, and a deploy puts that revision's own there
changedFromV3: it can go into the world and play, as a real, visible, mortal character
it is told the world is small and was never meant to stay that way
what it is told to look for is no longer only what went wrong
it can rewrite part of a file instead of all of it
the world view is summarised, and the raw feed is narrower by default
it is told the real wall-clock limit, and can ask what is left of it
long turns can fire on a quiet world, hourly, three in a row at most
a turn that produces no output at all is still killed on the deadline
the terminal capitalises sentences and checks spelling
nothing the previous caretaker built is carried forward
